source.title: The Depth Ceiling: On the Limits of Large Language Models in Discovering Latent Planning
source.authors: Yi Xu; Philipp Jettkant; L. Ruis

record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests latent planning depth and reports both shallow successes and sharp failures at greater depths, refining the scope of claims about internal look-ahead. Its graph path-finding task is not the rhyme-word representation or intervention in V1.
record.gate_note: The study measures task performance and probes attention in graph path-finding. It does not test rhyming verse, decode future tokens from a single hidden state, intervene on a represented future token, or test pre-caching. The explicit-CoT and ICoT results are excluded from rows for latent planning because the planning behavior is deliberately taught.
record.test_reason: The paper measures how deep latent (single-forward-pass) multi-step planning goes on star-graph path-finding. The task is built so that above-random accuracy requires look-ahead and no local heuristic suffices. It reports successes at shallow depths and a sharp ceiling at greater depths. Its results therefore bear on V5 (look-ahead beyond verse, in multi-step reasoning) and on V6 (planning is shallow, or explained by heuristics). Fine-tuning supervises only the final answer, not the planning steps. Zero-/few-shot results on pre-trained models show the behaviour arising without task training. So this is not induced behaviour. The paper has no rhyme, future-token decoding or pre-caching experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Models trained with final-answer-only supervision discover latent planning only to a shallow ceiling: 3 steps from scratch, 5 for fine-tuned GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B, 7 for GPT-5.4 few-shot. Scale improves breadth more than depth. Discovered strategies generalize up to 8 steps at test time. Explicit CoT supervision removes the bottleneck. The authors take this as support for chain-of-thought monitoring, while noting that broader domains are untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains or evaluates models on graph path-finding and probes attention; it does not use rhyme prompts or intervene on candidate rhyme-word representations.
record.method_sensitivity: Planning depth and branch factor change success. Few-shot prompting extends GPT-5.4's LPC from 5 to 7, but it fails at 8. Model size/family changes breadth and the depth ceiling; tested architecture scaling of the scratch transformer does not remove its m=4 failure.
record.code_released: not stated (the paper says data and scripts will be released publicly upon acceptance)
record.problems: The task is synthetic star-graph path-finding, so broader-domain generalization is untested. GPT-4o and GPT-5.4 test sets contain 100 samples; the authors cannot fine-tune GPT-5.4. Attention analysis is a probe and does not establish causal use of the measured attention pattern. The paper notes its results do not settle whether similar ceilings hold in other reasoning tasks.
record.rows_left_out: The tables report many additional model-by-depth-by-branch-factor skill values, zero-shot and few-shot settings, and architectural ablations. They are omitted to stay within the row limit and emphasize depth-ceiling successes and failures. In particular, Table 4 has further fine-tuned configurations; Tables 5–7 contain other ablation and prompting conditions; Table 1 has additional BR entries; and Figure 2 reports further out-of-distribution results. Explicit-CoT and ICoT results are omitted because those procedures deliberately teach or induce the planning behavior.

untested.parts: Chess, Sokoban and other domains. Mechanistic or causal evidence of look-ahead representations: only attention ratios and behaviour are measured.
Whether plans in free generation reach only a few tokens ahead. Whether plans steer generation, since no intervention is done. Settings beyond symmetric star graphs.
Not tested: no verse or rhyme.
Not tested: no decoding of future tokens from hidden states.

missing.what: Control showing that depth, not graph size, drives failure: GPT-4o fails G(2,6) (13 nodes) but solves the larger G(10,3).
Zero-shot latent planning capacity of pre-trained models without task training: Qwen3-8B 3, GPT-4o 4, GPT-5.4 5. Only GPT-5.4 has rows, yet these are the cleanest 'arising without training' results.
Fine-tuned discovery ceilings of Qwen2.5-32B and Qwen3-8B (m=4).

record.verdict_notes: Row states are written relative to V5. For V6 the depth-failure rows count as supporting evidence, and the success rows count against the heuristic explanation only. The V6 link is approximate: the paper measures depth of latent computation steps, not how many tokens ahead a plan reaches in free generation. The GPT-4o row of Table 4 is garbled in the text extraction, so its individual cells cannot be verified; r11 and r12 rest on the text. Explicit-CoT and ICoT results are correctly excluded as taught behaviour.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyme-word representations and interventions changing verse lines.
Decodability of tokens several positions ahead from a single hidden state.
Whether features are computed early because they help later positions, rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction.
Rhyme planning in smaller open-weight models and open attribution-graph or probing tools.
Chess and Sokoban; other reasoning domains beyond the graph path-finding task studied here.
Whether the reported depth limits or mechanisms generalize beyond star-graph path-finding.

relationships.condition: Star-graph path-finding at shallow depths (m=3 for the scratch transformer; up to m=5 fine-tuned; up to m=7 for GPT-5.4 few-shot)
relationships.reason: Above-random skill, which by design requires multi-step latent look-ahead (r1, r3, r7, r9, r11, r13, r14). Path-focused attention (r4) and generalization beyond training depth (r17).
relationships.display_finding: Performance exceeded chance at depth 3 for the scratch transformer, up to depth 5 after fine-tuning, and up to depth 7 for few-shot GPT-5.4, with path-focused attention and generalization beyond training depth.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Greater planning depth, and high branching for the scratch transformer
source_check.reason: Planning fails at greater depths; the scratch transformer also fails at k=10 because it cannot acquire even the neighbor heuristic.

relationships.reason: Latent planning is bounded at a few steps: discovery ceiling 3–5 and 7 few-shot, with abrupt failure one step deeper. Out-of-distribution generalization decays with depth (r2, r8, r10, r12, r15, r16, r17).
relationships.display_finding: Discovery ceilings were 3–5 steps and 7 with few-shot examples, with abrupt failure one step deeper and declining out-of-distribution generalization as depth increased.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Discovery ceilings and declining out-of-depth generalization support the shallow-planning clause under sparse final-answer supervision.

relationships.condition: The 'explained by local heuristics' part, on a task built to admit no local heuristic
relationships.reason: Perfect skill at m=3 cannot come from local cues (r1, r3). Attention traces the target-to-source path (r4, correlational). 95% of out-of-depth errors fall on the correct branch, unlike checkpoints still at the heuristic stage (r18).
relationships.display_finding: Perfect performance at m=3 could not rely on local cues, attention traced target-to-source paths, and 95% of out-of-depth errors stayed on the correct branch.

source_check.notes: Depth measures graph-planning steps, not future-token offsets; attention evidence is correlational. The source itself is inconsistent: abstract/introduction give an eight-step generalization ceiling, while Section 4 reports GPT-4o reaching m*+4 with m*=5.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Star-graph path-finding with next-token training or latent evaluation
reader_labels.reason: The study reports above-random latent planning on this non-verse task, including shallow successes and limited generalization beyond training depth (r1, r3, r7, r9, r11, r13, r14, r17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Performance has a depth ceiling: the scratch transformer fails at m=4, fine-tuned models fail beyond their reported ceilings, and GPT-5.4 few-shot fails at m=8 (r2, r10, r12, r15, r16).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Shallow graph-planning depths and successful transformer settings
reader_labels.reason: The study finds real but bounded latent planning, and elevated path-focused attention in a successful configuration, rather than only a local-neighbor heuristic (r1, r3, r4, r7, r9, r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Greater graph-planning depths and some evaluation settings
reader_labels.reason: Latent planning fails abruptly beyond several tested depth ceilings; few-shot prompting extends GPT-5.4's ceiling but does not remove it, and Qwen 2.5-7B's out-of-depth errors are mostly on-path (r2, r8, r10, r12, r15, r17, r18).
